report.headline: Usage rate projected to jump from 18.4% to 23.8% in the EuroLeague, but the true shooting projection is not trustworthy for this transition

projection.text: The model projects a usage rate of 23.8% in the EuroLeague, up from 18.4% in the NBA source season and above the EuroLeague's minutes-weighted average of 20.3%, consistent with a near-full transfer (slope 0.977) of the player's standing above their own league.

risks.text: The true shooting projection of 56.5% should not be trusted: the model's out-of-fold error (4.5%) is worse than the trivial league-mean baseline's error (4.3%) for this metric.
Even setting aside the shooting metric's unreliability, the wide 80%/95% usage intervals (19.4-28.2% / 17.1-30.5%) mean this is a group-level ranking tool, not a precise individual forecast.
The player was 30 years old in the source season, an older profile than typical for this kind of move.
A source-season turnover rate of 15.0% is a moderate risk given the projected increase in usage to 23.8%.

strengths.text: Usage rate is projected to rise well above the EuroLeague average (23.8% vs 20.3%), and the usage model itself is validated: its out-of-fold error of 3.2% beats the best trivial baseline's 4.2%.
The source season combined a 15.4% assist rate with 5.889 rebounds per 75 possessions, indicating a well-rounded statistical profile heading into the move.
Source-season true shooting of 56.7% sat 0.51 standard deviations above the NBA average that year, reflecting efficient scoring on a below-average usage rate of 18.4%.
The usage projection rests on a substantial historical base of 115 NBA-to-EuroLeague transitions.

uncertainty.text: The 80% prediction interval for usage rate runs from 19.4% to 28.2% and the 95% interval from 17.1% to 30.5%; against a EuroLeague usage standard deviation of 4.4%, that 80% band alone spans roughly two standard deviations of the league distribution, so the model can rank this player above average but cannot pin down where within that range he lands.
